# Florida sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over AI risks

It is the first such lawsuit to be filed by a state against OpenAI and Sam Altman.

![Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier speaks during a ceremony on May 20, 2026, in Miami, Florida. ](https://www.politico.com/dims4/default/resize/630/quality/90/format/webp?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstatic.politico.com%2F06%2F2f%2F9f22c7ee4e828fc2824139b88b76%2Fhttps-delivery-gettyimages.com%2Fdownloads%2F2276715392)

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier speaks during a ceremony on May 20, 2026, in Miami, Florida. \| Eva Marie Uzcategui/Getty Images

By [Aaron Mak](https://www.politico.com/staff/aaron-mak), [Andrew Atterbury](https://www.politico.com/staff/andrew-atterbury) and [Hassan Ali Kanu](https://www.politico.com/staff/hassan-ali-kanu)06/01/2026 11:38 AM EDTUpdated: 06/01/2026 12:08 PM EDT

- [Facebook (opens in a new window)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://politi.co/4fYLpCq)
- [X (opens in a new window)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https://politi.co/4fYLpCq&text=Florida%20sues%20OpenAI%20and%20Sam%20Altman%20over%20AI%20risks&via=politico)

Florida Republican Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a lawsuit on Monday against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman, alleging that the AI startup’s ChatGPT is unsafe and that the company misled the public about associated risks.

The suit contends that ChatGPT poses risks to children and is responsible for a “litany of harms,” including addiction and aiding and abetting mass shootings and suicide. It seeks civil penalties for alleged violations of the state’s unfair trade practice, product liability, public nuisance and negligence laws.

“\[T\]he rise of OpenAI is attributable to a web of deceit and the exploitation of users (including Floridians), leveraging their data and safety to boost OpenAI’s market value at unacceptable costs,” the complaint reads.

It is the first such action against OpenAI and Altman by a state, and follows a slew of recent product liability lawsuits against Big Tech companies.

“I hope and expect other states will follow and ultimately we need \[AI companies\] to change their programming,” Uthmeier said Monday during a press conference announcing the lawsuit in West Palm Beach. The attorney general highlighted a 2025 mass shooting that was allegedly committed with the assistance of ChatGPT, saying prosecutors believed that they could have brought additional conspiracy charges if the perpetrators’ conversations with the AI program had instead involved another person.

On June 1, 2026, local time, Attorney General James Usmayer filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman, alleging that the company deliberately released ChatGPT to the public, including children, while concealing significant risks, suppressing internal safety warnings, and deceiving Florida residents about the true nature and dangers of the product.

Attorney General Ousmayer explained, 'Today we announced the first state-led lawsuit in the nation against OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman. # Stock Market News, June 2, 2026: Investors Weigh AI Fervor Against Mideast Worries

## Stocks close at fresh records for fifth straight session

Stocks ended slightly higher after another tug-of-war day for markets as artificial-intelligence fever contended with Mideast disquiet.

U.S. stock indexes rose less than 0.5% as investors digested more AI news, starting with the prospect of eyewatering equity issues: Anthropic filed for its initial public offering, while Google parent Alphabet [is looking to raise $80 billion](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-06-02-2026/card/how-google-s-80-billion-equity-plan-compares-to-the-biggest-ever-RouOGMQ35qa606Uq4DRC). Alphabet investors didn't love the idea of all that new spending and sent the shares 3.9% lower.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock, however, soared 19% after the server company reported rampant AI demand, and Marvell Technology jumped 33% on hopes it could become [the next $1 trillion company](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-06-02-2026/card/marvell-stock-soars-after-nvidia-s-huang-says-it-could-be-next-1-trillion-company-KJinU0UtqRAQdM7CCT64).

Industrials such as Caterpillar performed well, driving the Dow Jones Industrial Average up 229 points, or 0.4%. All three indexes finished at records for the fifth consecutive trading session, a feat last achieved in 2017, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

# UK banks blocked from cyber AI tool Mythos get offer from rival OpenAI

1 day ago

Share

Save

[Add as preferred on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=bbc.com)

Zoe KleinmanTechnology editor

![Reuters View of the major buildings of the City of London, headquarters to many financial firms, at dawn. The low sun off screen to the right illuminates the facades of the many multistorey skyscrapers, with the turrets of the Tower of London in the foreground.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/1da9/live/87ea54d0-5dae-11f1-8132-9508271dd882.jpg.webp)Reuters

OpenAI has offered nine major UK banks access to its cyber security AI tool GPT-5.5 Cyber, as its fierce rival Anthropic has blocked them in previews of its version, Claude Mythos.

Both tools are designed to find hidden security weaknesses in digital systems and can outperform humans at some hacking and cyber-security tasks.

Mythos caused a stir when it was announced in April, with Anthropic claiming it had found a weakness in one legacy system which had remained hidden for nearly 30 years.

Some finance ministers, central bankers and financiers have since [expressed serious concerns about it](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2ev24yx4rmo), fearing the model could undermine the security of all financial systems.

![PA Media Governor of the Bank of England Andrew Bailey sits on a stage, addressing the audience and gesturing with an open hand. He wears a dark suit, white shirt, dark tie and glasses.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/b24c/live/e1900200-5dae-11f1-8132-9508271dd882.jpg.webp)PA Media

Governor of the Bank of England Andrew Bailey said last week UK banks still could not access Mythos, Anthropic's AI model

The AI Security Institute, which has tested both Anthropic's Mythos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Cyber, said in its report that they reached "a similar level of performance" in the tasks it set them.

Last week Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned that UK banks were still unable to access Mythos to test the security of their own digital systems and apps.

# June Android Drop: Quick Share AirDrop expansion, AI in Play Books, & more, Android 17 coming soon

[![Avatar for Abner Li](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/d8da06fcba2b80ec1f2d301d7376dae8e055ac48d88994a8042b1d6b2c352534?s=30&d=mm&r=r)](https://9to5google.com/author/technacity/) [Abner Li](https://9to5google.com/author/technacity/ "Posts by Abner Li") \| Jun 2 2026 - 11:00 am PT

[13 Comments](https://9to5google.com/2026/06/02/june-2026-android-drop/#comments)

![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/03/android-figure-mwc-galaxy-xr-workbench.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600)

Google today [announced](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/platforms/android/Android-Drop-June-2026/) the latest spring features with the June Android Drop. At the same time, Google teased that “even more exciting updates \[are\] coming soon in Android 17.”

**Related**: [Google Phone app rolling out Android fake call detection that uses RCS](https://9to5google.com/?p=716386)

Google is [continuing to expand](https://9to5google.com/2026/05/12/google-bringing-airdrop-support-most-android-phones-later-this-year/) **Quick Share’s** AirDrop compatibility. The latest supported devices are as follows:

- **Samsung**: Galaxy S25, S25+, S25 Ultra, S25 Edge, Galaxy Z Flip7, Z Fold7, Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy S24, Galaxy S24+, Galaxy S24 Ultra, Galaxy Z Flip6, Z Fold6, Z Fold6 (Special Edition)
- **OnePlus**: OnePlus 15
- **Xiaomi**: Xiaomi 17T Pro
- **Vivo**: Vivo X300 and X300 Pro
- **Honor**: Magic V6

**Google Play Books** is adding an AI-powered “Book insights” feature. When you zoom out of a page, there’s a new light bulb badged by the Gemini spark in the top-right corner. Tapping opens the Book insights chat page where you can “Ask Play Books” with a “Catch me up” recap prompt. You can also “highlight a passage to ask questions and dive deeper into themes, context or characters.”

# Amazon Web Services event explores AI and security for research

AWS event at the U highlights security, AI and new tools to optimize research.

[![AWS Principal Solutions Architect, Dr. Claudiu Farcas, discusses Amazon Quick at the University of Utah on Wednesday, May 27th, 2026. (Photo by Kristina Walker | The Daily Utah Chronicle)](https://dailyutahchronicle.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/W264979-1200x800.jpg)](https://dailyutahchronicle.com/2026/06/01/amazon-web-services-event-explores-ai-and-security-for-research/#photo)

[Kristina Walker](https://dailyutahchronicle.com/staff_name/kristina-walker/)

AWS Principal Solutions Architect, Dr. Claudiu Farcas, discusses Amazon Quick at the University of Utah on Wednesday, May 27th, 2026. (Photo by Kristina Walker \| The Daily Utah Chronicle)

By [Meadow Stewart](https://dailyutahchronicle.com/staff_name/meadow-stewart/), News Writer

June 1, 2026

University of Utah researchers gathered on May 27-28 for a [two-day workshop](https://www.research.utah.edu/) that focused on using secure cloud technologies to protect sensitive data and understanding how AI functions in academic research.

The Office of the Vice President for Research [Security Office](https://security.research.utah.edu/) hosted the event in partnership with [Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/). The event introduced faculty, researchers, scientists and IT professionals to tools designed for data-intensive research with AI. There were presentations, demonstrations and hands-on workshops where attendees learned how to use AI tools to automate work and meet federal compliance requirements.

### **Research through security and compliance**

The workshop aimed to help researchers understand how these technologies can support both innovation and compliance. “We are in a new, great new world,” Dr. Erin Rothwell, the [vice president for research](https://www.research.utah.edu/meet-the-vpr/), said. “Things are going to be more data-intensive, more AI-enabled, and more highly collaborative, and so with that, it is going to be more highly regulated.”

Rothwell said research security is becoming a large part of maintaining a federal research portfolio. “If you want to stay competitive for federal grants, you need to have a real research security office,” she said.
